### Agenda

## Editors’ Discussion
- Do we want to move `Call for Input` Issues to ethereum/pm for increased visibility?
- How should we best handle open PRs in the [EIPs](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs) & [ERCs](https://github.com/ethereum/ERCs) repo?

- [Topics suggested](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1777#issuecomment-3575593807) and [here](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1777#issuecomment-3665986257) by @jochem-brouwer 
- Restructure & rename EIPIP meeting
  - Extend invitation to the Ethereum Governance team from EF, client devs, along with EIP Editors.
  - Rename ot to ACD-G with a once-a-month cadence
  - Agenda to share & discuss present process & potential concerns. Support and guidance can help streamline the new upgrade process.
- PRs for Editors review and/or consensus

    - https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/10319
    - https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/10338
    - https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/10693
- From EIP Office Hour [76](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1775)

  - A collection of _EIP documentation formats_ for test cases and reference implementation at a canonical place for new authors to refer to.
- EIP-1 Updates & Editorial Policies: Follow up (any PRs from the last discussion?)
  - EIP-1 isn't updated on the [website](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1) with changes pushed with [PR](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/10466)

### EIPsInsight update
- EIP board page updated based on Sam's recommendations from the last EIPIP meeting.

We might have to discuss the idea of adding which fork an EIP was added in to some service (eips.ethereum.org for instance). I believe it will be useful, but:
I think an EIP can be Final without being in a fork. But this raises question what Final EIPs are actually part of the consensus (either now or in the past).

 We also have EIPs which can retroactively be filled, for instance https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-684. This rule is active, but what fork did it get added? I believe it should also be added to the Meta EIP of that fork.

I proposed this EIP for Glamsterdam: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7610, because I believe that all clients support it but that this never has been made "officially" part of the spec. So this is also one of the reasons why we would like a complete list of all EIPs in the forks/spec, for clarity, also for the ACD process because it has been brought up that this EIP is already included/supported by clients, but I think ACD should then make it clear that this is part of the spec (and for retroactively fillable EIPs this should likely be part of the Frontier/Chainstart spec. What would this be? An older version of the yellow paper?)

I posted this here for visibility, but maybe I should move these discussions to magicians. Is there a thread about this feature?

Other note: issue title notes Dec 17, but in the description of this issue it also says: 

> Next meeting - Dec 19 at 1600 UTC

> Other note: issue title notes Dec 17, but in the description of this issue it also says:
> 
> > Next meeting - Dec 19 at 1600 UTC

Thanks for flag, fixed!

Maybe a final topic I want to add last minute (can also discuss this async):

I just got added as EIP editor. If I thus approve a PR it means I approve it for the editorial part (because new EIPs will then get merged). However an approval can (a GitHub review approval), I believe, signal 3 different things:

- Editorial approval (EIP follows the rules we have set for the format, as specified in EIP-1)
- Reviewal approval (EIP makes technical sense, and the direct obstacles are removed or addressed in the EIP)
- Or, more general: an approval (which some people do) signal support for the EIP to get merged in a fork

I believe these 3 are different things. For the editorial/review part, I wonder if it makes sense to instead use a different account (for me) for the editorial process so it is clear what part I approve of (either point 1, or point 2 (and maybe 3)). This is because I also review EIPs from a technical perspective.
